_about: Controlled vocabulary for architectures.json. `modules` lists the course modules that teach the part today (from course/README.md and module READMEs, survey of 2026-11-14); an empty list marks a gap the explorer would be first to fill. Module numbers come from a grep of module READMEs for each term, so a number means the README names the part, not that it teaches it in depth. Records use these ids in attention.kind, attention.mixers, attention.other, attention.sparse.kind, attention.position.scheme and scaling, attention.qk_norm, layer_kinds mixer/ffn/position, norm.kind, ffn.kind, ffn.activation, block_order steps, specials, tokenizer.kind and teaches; validate.py rejects any other value except the sentinels 'none' (no such part) and 'mixed' (position scheme differs by layer kind; see layer_kinds). norm.placement keeps its short values (pre, post, sandwich, post_in_residual), which map to pre_norm, post_norm, sandwich_norm, post_in_residual. `aliases` lists ids merged into a term; records must use the term's id.

groups.mixer: how a token gathers information from other tokens
groups.precision: number formats the weights ship in

terms.name: Token embedding
terms.def: A table that turns each token id into a vector of width d_model.

terms.name: Tied embeddings
terms.def: The output layer reuses the input embedding table, saving its parameters.

terms.name: Residual connection
terms.def: Each sublayer adds its output to a running sum that flows through the whole stack.

terms.name: Output head
terms.def: A matrix that maps the last vector to one score per vocabulary entry.

terms.name: Attention residuals (depth attention)
terms.def: Instead of adding all earlier outputs equally, each sublayer reads a learned weighted mix of earlier block outputs.

terms.name: Parallel attention and MLP
terms.def: Attention and MLP read the same input and their outputs are summed, instead of running one after the other.

terms.name: Per-layer output scalar
terms.def: Each layer's output is multiplied by its own stored scalar.

terms.name: Gated residual
terms.def: Each residual add becomes a learned per-channel weighted mix of the stream and the sublayer output.

terms.name: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections
terms.def: The residual stream is kept as several parallel copies (4 in DeepSeek V4) that a Sinkhorn-normalised matrix mixes around each sublayer.

terms.name: Causal encoder-decoder split
terms.def: A decoder-only stack cut in two: the first half reads the prompt causally and its final states give the second half's global keys and values.

terms.name: Multi-head attention
terms.def: Every head has its own queries, keys and values.

terms.name: Multi-query attention
terms.def: All query heads share one key head and one value head, shrinking the cache.

terms.name: Grouped-query attention
terms.def: Query heads split into groups; each group shares one key and value head.

terms.name: Multi-head latent attention
terms.def: Keys and values are stored as one small compressed vector per token and expanded when used.

terms.name: Sliding-window attention
terms.def: A token attends only to the last W tokens, so cache and cost stop growing with length.

terms.name: Local/global interleave
terms.def: Most layers use a short window; every n-th layer sees the whole context.

terms.name: Top-k sparse attention (DSA and kin)
terms.def: A cheap indexer scores past tokens and full attention runs only on the best k.

terms.name: Linear attention
terms.def: Replaces the attention matrix with a running summary, so cost grows linearly with length.

terms.name: Gated DeltaNet
terms.def: Linear attention whose memory matrix is corrected by a delta rule and decays through a gate.

terms.name: Kimi Delta Attention
terms.def: A Gated DeltaNet variant with a finer per-channel gate, used by Kimi Linear and K3.

terms.name: Selective state-space layer (Mamba)
terms.def: A recurrent layer with a fixed-size state whose update depends on the input.

terms.name: RWKV time-mix
terms.def: A recurrent mixer trained like a transformer and run like an RNN.

terms.name: mLSTM (xLSTM)
terms.def: An LSTM with a matrix memory and exponential gates, used in place of attention.

terms.name: Short convolution
terms.def: A depthwise convolution over the last few tokens (kernel 3 or 4) that mixes local context cheaply.

terms.name: Hybrid stack
terms.def: A stack that mixes attention layers with recurrent, linear, convolution or compressed-attention layers.

terms.name: Chunked attention
terms.def: Tokens attend only inside fixed blocks of C tokens; unlike a sliding window, the span restarts at each block boundary.

terms.name: Cross-layer KV sharing
terms.def: Some layers reuse the keys and values of an earlier layer instead of computing their own, which shrinks the cache.

terms.name: Compressed sparse attention (CSA)
terms.def: Groups of past keys and values are pooled into one entry each; an indexer picks the top k entries, and a short window of recent tokens stays uncompressed.

terms.name: Heavily compressed attention (HCA)
terms.def: Every m past tokens (128 in DeepSeek V4) are pooled into one entry and all entries are attended, plus a short uncompressed window.

terms.name: Compressed sparse attention 2 (CSA2)
terms.def: DeepSeek V4.1's CSA in which groups of layers share one layer's compressed keys and values and reuse or re-rank its top-k picks.

terms.name: Token shift
terms.def: Each position mixes its input with the previous token's input before the projections (RWKV).

terms.name: Data-dependent decay
terms.def: The per-channel decay of a recurrent state is computed from the current input instead of being fixed.

terms.name: Learned absolute positions
terms.def: A trained vector per position is added to the token embedding; no use past the trained length.

terms.name: Rotary position embedding (RoPE)
terms.def: Rotates query and key pairs by an angle that grows with position, so scores depend on distance.

terms.name: Partial RoPE
terms.def: Only a share of each head's dimensions is rotated; the rest carry no position.

terms.name: ALiBi
terms.def: Adds a penalty to attention scores in proportion to distance; no position vectors.

terms.name: Learned relative-position bias
terms.def: A learned term, a function of the distance between two tokens, is added to their score.

terms.name: No positional encoding (NoPE)
terms.def: The layer gets no position signal; the causal mask alone tells order.

terms.name: YaRN
terms.def: Rescales RoPE frequencies so a model trained short can read longer contexts.

terms.name: Position interpolation
terms.def: Divides positions by a factor so a longer input maps into the trained range.

terms.name: Llama 3 RoPE scaling
terms.def: Stretches low RoPE frequencies and keeps high ones, to extend context to 128K.

terms.name: Log-length attention scaling
terms.def: Multiplies attention scores by a factor that grows with the log of context length.

terms.name: Multimodal RoPE (M-RoPE)
terms.def: Rotary dimensions are split into sections for time, height and width, so image and video tokens get 2D or 3D positions.

terms.name: LeRoPE
terms.def: A learned factor per frequency rescales the RoPE frequencies.

terms.name: LayerNorm
terms.def: Subtracts the mean and divides by the spread of each vector, then rescales.

terms.name: RMSNorm
terms.def: Divides each vector by its root-mean-square, with no mean subtraction; cheaper than LayerNorm.

terms.name: Post-norm
terms.def: Normalise after adding the sublayer output to the residual (original 2017 transformer).

terms.name: Pre-norm
terms.def: Normalise the sublayer input; the residual path itself is never normalised.

terms.name: Sandwich norm
terms.def: Normalise both the input and the output of each sublayer before the residual add.

terms.name: Post-norm inside the residual
terms.def: Normalise the sublayer output, then add it to an un-normalised residual (OLMo 2 style).

terms.name: Embedding norm
terms.def: A norm applied to the token embeddings before the first layer.

terms.name: Zero-centred RMSNorm
terms.def: RMSNorm whose weight is stored as an offset from 1 and applied as (1 + w), so weight decay pulls it toward 1.

terms.name: Per-head output norm
terms.def: The output of each head is normalised on its own before the heads are joined.

terms.name: Plain MLP
terms.def: Two matrices with a nonlinearity between, usually four times wider inside.

terms.name: Gated linear unit
terms.def: Two parallel projections; one, passed through a nonlinearity, scales the other.

terms.name: ReLU
terms.def: Keeps positive values, zeroes negative ones.

terms.name: GELU
terms.def: A smooth ReLU that weights each input by the chance a normal variable is below it.

terms.name: GELU (tanh approximation)
terms.def: GELU computed with a tanh formula; GPT-2's gelu_new.

terms.name: SwiGLU
terms.def: A gated unit whose gate uses SiLU (x times sigmoid x).

terms.name: GeGLU
terms.def: A gated unit whose gate uses GELU (Gemma).

terms.name: SiTU-GLU
terms.def: A gated unit with Moonshot's SiTU gate function; the config names it 'situ'.

terms.name: MLP soft-capping
terms.def: tanh caps on the gate and up projections inside the feed-forward part.

terms.name: Squared ReLU
terms.def: Keeps positive values and squares them; zeroes negative ones.

terms.name: Mixture of experts
terms.def: Many feed-forward experts; a router sends each token to a few, so only part of the model runs per token.

terms.name: Router
terms.def: A small layer that scores experts for each token and keeps the top k.

terms.name: Shared expert
terms.def: An expert every token uses, beside the routed ones.

terms.name: Fine-grained experts
terms.def: Many small experts with more chosen per token, instead of a few large ones.

terms.name: Dense first layers
terms.def: The first one to three layers keep an ordinary FFN before MoE layers start.

terms.name: LatentMoE
terms.def: Tokens are projected to a narrower width before the routed experts and back after.

terms.name: Dense MLP beside MoE
terms.def: A dense MLP runs in parallel with the routed experts in every layer (Grok).

terms.name: Hash routing
terms.def: Experts are chosen from a fixed table indexed by token id, not by a learned router.

terms.name: Logit soft-capping
terms.def: Squashes scores with tanh so none can grow past a fixed cap.

terms.name: Attention sink
terms.def: A learned slot a head can put weight on when no real token deserves it.

terms.name: Gated attention output
terms.def: A sigmoid gate computed from the input scales the attention output per channel.

terms.name: QK-norm
terms.def: Normalises queries and keys per head before their dot product, which steadies training.

terms.name: L2 clipping of queries and keys
terms.def: Caps the length of query and key vectors instead of normalising them.

terms.name: Multi-token prediction
terms.def: Extra small layers predict tokens further ahead; used in training and as a draft model for faster decoding.

terms.name: Engram n-gram memory
terms.def: Large lookup tables indexed by recent n-grams, read by a few layers (DeepSeek V4.1).

terms.name: Per-layer embeddings
terms.def: Each layer gets its own small token embedding, stored off the accelerator (Gemma E models).

terms.name: Custom attention scale
terms.def: Scores are divided by a set constant instead of the square root of head size.

terms.name: Attention soft-capping
terms.def: Squashes attention scores with tanh so none can pass a fixed cap (Gemma 2: 50, Grok: 30).

terms.name: Gate soft-capping
terms.def: Caps the input and forget gate pre-activations of a recurrent cell with tanh (xLSTM: 15).

terms.name: Output scaling
terms.def: The last hidden state or the logits are multiplied by a fixed constant before the softmax.

terms.name: Embedding scaling
terms.def: Token embeddings are multiplied by a constant, often the square root of d_model, before the first layer.

terms.name: No bias terms
terms.def: Linear layers carry weights only, no added bias vectors.

terms.name: QKV bias
terms.def: Query, key and value projections carry bias terms while other linear layers do not.

terms.name: Keys reused as values
terms.def: A layer projects keys only and uses them as values too, so it stores one tensor instead of two.

terms.name: Virtual head attention
terms.def: A low-rank mix across attention heads, with an identity skip, applied to the head outputs.

terms.name: Multimax output head
terms.def: The output head applies a learned temperature that changes piecewise with the logit value.

terms.name: Scaled residual initialisation
terms.def: Weights of layers that write into the residual stream start smaller, by 1/sqrt(N) for N such layers.

terms.name: Document masking
terms.def: During training, tokens may not attend across the boundary between documents packed into one sequence.

terms.name: z-loss
terms.def: A training penalty on the log of the softmax normaliser that keeps output logits from drifting large.

terms.name: QK-clip (MuonClip)
terms.def: During training, query and key weights are scaled down whenever an attention score grows past a threshold.

terms.name: Rolling KV cache
terms.def: The KV cache holds only the last W positions; position i overwrites slot i mod W.

terms.name: Grouped output projection
terms.def: Attention outputs are projected in groups through a low-rank step before the final projection to d_model.

terms.name: Vision encoder
terms.def: A separate network (often a ViT such as SigLIP) that turns image patches into vectors the decoder reads.

terms.name: Audio encoder
terms.def: Turns sound into vectors or discrete tokens the decoder reads.

terms.name: Byte-level BPE
terms.def: Merges frequent byte pairs into tokens; any text can be encoded.

terms.name: SentencePiece
terms.def: A tokenizer library that trains BPE or unigram vocabularies on raw text.

terms.name: tiktoken BPE
terms.def: OpenAI's fast byte-level BPE format, reused by Llama 3, Kimi and Inkling.

terms.name: 4-bit floats (MXFP4, NVFP4, FP4)
terms.def: 4-bit floating-point numbers with a shared scale per small block of values; used for expert weights and, in DeepSeek V4.1, the KV cache.
